question.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$L=[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ -9 & -11\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $L-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
L-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 6 \\ -9 & -11-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(L-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(L-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 6 \\ -9 & -11-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )(-11-\lambda )-6\cdot (-9) & =0 \\ -33-3\lambda +11\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+54 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+8\lambda +21 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the discriminant of the quadratic equation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={8}^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 21 \\  & =64-84 \\  & =-20 \\  & <0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the characteristic equation does not have real solutions and therefore $L$ does not have real eigenvalues.
